It invokes the seven marked-word erasers,the two marker removals and four bare-stream erasers with every transfer paid. Its exact budget is the sum of marked-word and stream erasure costs plus paid transfers. For a canonical input of length P=inputLength(n),n>=1,and a dimension word of value n and length n.size,the total cost is at most C_F*P,where C_F depends only on the fixed rational map family. Stream lengths are bounded using previously proved paid generation traces; equal-length binary value uniqueness identifies their dimension words. Thus no uncharged length oracle or implicit erasure is used. This is a prepared-endpoint cleanup theorem,not yet the integrated blank-start paid prefix.
